purpose: Irbesartan is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to protect the kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes who have high blood pressure. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps your heart, blood vessels, and kidneys stay healthier for longer.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises your blood pressure. Irbesartan blocks the receptors that this chemical attaches to, so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a safer level.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly. Tiredness or feeling fatigued. Upset stomach, nausea, or diarrhea. Headache. Muscle or joint aches. Unlike some similar medications, irbesartan usually does NOT cause a dry cough.
warnings: Do NOT take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm or even be fatal to an unborn baby. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor approves, as this drug can raise potassium levels. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems. Do not take it with aliskiren if you have diabetes. Always stand up slowly to avoid dizziness from a sudden drop in blood pressure.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 150 mg once daily, taken with or without food. Your doctor may increase this to 300 mg once daily if needed for better blood pressure control. Try to take it at the same time each day, and never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
